MSU: Subawards vs. Subcontracts

From the ORA eTraining module "Purchasing with Purpose: Procurement on Sponsored Projects" (lesson 7 of 15).
What Is a Subaward?
A subaward typically occurs when a primary grantee or institution receives federal funding and then further distributes a portion of those funds to a collaborating entity, often a subrecipient, to perform specific project-related tasks or activities. Subawards are usually utilized when the collaborating institution has a significant role in the project's design, conduct, or outcomes and they are responsible for their own compliance with federal regulations. In contrast, a subcontract is a contractual arrangement where a portion of the federal grant is allocated to a third-party organization or entity to provide specific goods or services related to the research project. Subcontracts are typically used when the collaborating entity is rendering specialized services and operates under the direct oversight of the primary grantee, who maintains control over the research direction and compliance obligations.
A subaward ( 2CFR200.331 ) is issued when a portion of a sponsored project is carried out by another organization that is acting as a subrecipient . In this arrangement, the external entity is responsible for performing a substantive portion of the programmatic work and contributes to overall project objectives. A subcontract (a.k.a. a contractor/vendor agreement ) is used when an external entity is engaged to provide goods and services that support a sponsored project, but does not take part in the programmatic direction or intellectual leadership of the work. The distinction between subawardee and subcontractor should be made prior to proposal submission. Any new subawards created during the performance period of the prime award will require sponsor approval.

Subawards: MSU as the Prime
When Morgan State University receives an award directly from a sponsor and intends to have another institution complete a portion of the project work, MSU serves as the prime recipient and must establish a subaward with that outside entity. A subaward allows the subrecipient to carry out part of the sponsored project while MSU remains responsible for the overall award, including sponsor compliance, monitoring, invoice review, and ensuring the work aligns with the approved scope and budget.
Subaward Setup with MSU as Prime

Pre-Award: Identify Collaborators
The prospective PI at MSU speaks with colleagues outside of MSU regarding the potential to partner on a grant together. MSU will be designated as the Prime and the outside individual (potentially Co-PI) and their institution/organization will be the Subrecipient.
https://articulateusercontent.com/assets/rise/assets/block-defaults/sky_mountains_thumb.jpg
Discuss Project Specifics with the Subrecipient
The PI and their collaborator will discuss the specifics of the project goals, potential expenses, etc. After coming up with (a) a framework for what the project will entail and (b) a detailed budget, the PI will complete the Internal Routing Form (IRF) available through the Office of Research Administration webpage. The PI will then work with Ms. Ailing Zhang and Ms. Deshun Li on the proposal submission and budget preparation and justification. Indirect Cost (IDC) charges for MSU will be assessed on the first $25,000 of the full subaward project budget. The remainder of the agreement does not result in indirect cost charges. If this is a multi-year agreement, and the subawardee will work with MSU for all project years without interruption, then IDC will be assessed only on the first $25,000 of Year 1. The subawardee's institution will charge its own IDC, separate from MSU's.
Subawardee Will Draft Associated Documentation
While the PI works with the ORA staff on budget and proposal prep activities, the subrecipient institution will draft the following documentation: Letter of Commitment Detailed Budget & Budget Justification covering all years of the agreement Statement of Work Subrecipient Commitment Form These forms are available at the bottom of this lesson.
Submitting the Project Proposal
Once the subrecipient has completed the documents mentioned in Step 3, Ms. Ailing Zhang will collect them and submit the proposal to the funding agency for review.
Post-Award: Submitting a Workflow Request
If awarded, the PI should submit a workflow request in Banner to ensure they have budget posting access to the project. The process for submitting a workflow request can be found here . Submitting the workflow access request would come after participating in an ORA Post-Award Briefing, which will result in RFA assigning Banner budget codes. This step is vital as without it the PI, or their admin, will be unable to submit a requisition in Banner to encumber the funds for the award. Without the requisition in place invoices CANNOT be paid!
Drafting the Subaward Agreement
If awarded, the PI should contact Matthew Lee to draft the subaward agreement. Mr. Lee will complete the following: Review documents outlined in Step 3, as well as ensure the Internal Routing Form (IRF) for the project has been completed. Utilize those documents to draft the subaward agreement and send the draft to the partner institution for review and signature. Perform an internal risk assessment to finalize reporting and invoicing requirements of the subawardee Upon receipt from the subrecipient, Mr. Lee will send the partially executed agreement to the VP of Finance and Management for review and final approval. This process typically takes 7-10 business days.
Drafting the Subaward Agreement (cont)
Once signed by the VP for Finance and Management, the agreement is considered fully executed and actionable. Mr. Lee will send the completion notice and copy of the agreement to the partner institution. He will also send the internal completion email to ORA and RFA. After the subaward agreement is fully executed the subawardee may begin work.
Create the Requisition
With the completed subaward agreement in hand, the PI must enter a requisition to encumber the subaward funds in their prime budget. If this is the first time MSU has worked with the subrecipient entity then a Vendor Registration Form will need to be completed and sent to the MSU Procurement team. Once received, Procurement will provide the PI with a MSU Vendor ID for requisition entry. The PI will enter a requisition in Banner for the total dollar amount of funding for that fiscal year or performance period. New requisitions will need to be submitted with each funding increment. The Procurement team will need a copy of the completed subaward agreement. Once in hand, they will convert the requisition to an authorized Purchase Order (PO).
Processing Subrecipient Invoices
The subrecipient will draft invoices for work performed under the project and submit them to the MSU PI. The PI will review the invoice and confirm that work and/or deliverables outlined by the charges in the invoice have been successfully completed. The PI will then authorize the invoice for payment and send the approved invoice to the MSU Accounts Payable department. To appropriately authorize an invoice the following should be written somewhere on the document: Write the statement "OK to Pay" Include the Purchase Order # Signature of an authorized individual (PI or their designee)
Renewal or Modification of the Subaward
Matthew Lee will draft a new agreement/modification for every performance period of the agreement. Similar signatures will be required here as with the initial agreement.

Subawards: MSU as the Sub
When another institution or organization receives an award directly from a sponsor and includes Morgan State University to perform a defined portion of the project work, that organization serves as the prime recipient, and MSU serves as the subrecipient . In this role, MSU is responsible for completing its assigned scope of work and complying with the terms provided by the prime recipient, while the prime recipient remains accountable to the sponsor for the overall award.
Subaward Setup with MSU as Subrecipient
Collaborate with Prime PI
Prospective PI at partner institution speaks with a colleague at MSU (co-PI) regarding the potential to partner on a grant together. The PI at the partner institution would be the prime recipient and MSU would act as the subrecipient.
The PI and their collaborator will discuss the specifics of the project goals, potential expenses, etc. After coming up with (a) a framework for what the project will entail and (b) a detailed budget, the MSU co-PI will complete the Internal Routing Form (IRF) for the subaward portion of the prime award. The co-PI will then work with Ms. Ailing Zhang, Ms. Deshun Li, and Mr. Matthew Lee on the proposal submission and budget preparation and justification.
Discuss Project Specifics with the Subrecipient (cont.)
At the same time, Mr. Lee will work with Ms. Zhang and the co-PI to draft the following documentation: Letter of Commitment Detailed Budget & Budget Justification ideally covering all years of the agreement Statement of Work FDP Clearinghouse Form The forms can be found below.
Contacting the Prime Institution
Once all paperwork is completed, Mr. Lee will contact the partner institution to provide the necessary paperwork for the agreeement. Once in hand, the partner institution will submit the proposal to the funding agency.
Finalizing the Subaward Agreement
If awarded, the partner institution should provide the draft subaward agreement to be reviewed by Mr. Lee and Mr. David LaChina (VP F&M). Mr. Lee and Mr. LaChina will review/sign the agreement and return it to the partner institution. The partner institution will then provide Mr. Lee with a copy of the fully executed agreement. The co-PI should also submit a workflow request in Banner to ensure they have budget posting access to the project. The process for submitting a workflow request can be found here . Submitting the workflow access request would come after participating in an ORA Post-Award Briefing, which will result in RFA assigning Banner budget codes. This step is vital as without it the PI, or their admin, will be unable to post expenses in Banner to invoice the Prime institution. Without Banner-posted expenses, RFA will be unable to effectively invoice the prime institution for your subaward's costs.
Spend The Funds & Get Paid
The co-PI must ensure they are spending down the budget and the expenses are tracked in Banner. The co-PI will also work with Restricted Funds Accounting (RFA) to ensure they are invoicing the prime institution in a timely manner for costs incurred by the co-PI's subagreement.
